tasks.short: Supervise engineers and crew, prepare training and record demonstrated competence.

steps.what: Review crew duties, training history and current procedures
Write routine and emergency training plans and exercise instructions
Assign routine duties and training exercise roles to crew
Brief engineers and crew on their duties and exercise roles
Supervise engineers and crew members during routine duties
Train crew for routine and emergency duties through instruction and practice
Record training participation, demonstrated competence and further coaching needs

tasks.design: Configure linked procedure views and training-plan templates in {DOCS}, with native outcome fields in {LMS}. Keep planning, assignments, briefing, supervision, practical training and post-training recording as distinct phases.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training plans and participation records repeat crew and procedure context.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and linked training fields can remove repeated clerical preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Attendance does not establish competence in an actual emergency.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unsafe practice and adapt coaching to demonstrated capability.
tasks.altitude: Keep practical supervision present while making training outcomes traceable.

reach.learn: Distinguish participation from demonstrated competence and open coaching needs.

evidence.claim: Native procedure views and training templates could reduce repeated planning and outcome entry; this crew-supervision saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Training preparation and post-training records are inside the task and separately priced from teaching and supervision.

The engineer produces procedure version, objectives, exercises and roles in s2, then crew identifier, date, participation, demonstrated performance and coaching needs in s7. Retained 10.5 and seven hours include capture and checks; incomplete competence evidence remains unresolved.
Try existing native templates and LMS fields first. No model allocates crew, assesses competence or sends a notification.
Colleague instruction stays internal. No self-approval gate or saving for a same-system save is proposed.
unknowns: Existing training templates and actual repeated entry time.
research_questions: Do linked templates reduce clerical work without turning attendance into a competence claim?

incremental.description: Maintain procedure links and training fields.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=90.5, gross=9.5; upkeep=2 gives central net=7.5. Practical supervision and training retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Liaise between captains and shore colleagues and record operational agreements.

steps.what: Retrieve ship schedules, budgets and outstanding operational issues
Clarify captains' and shore personnel's operational constraints
Reconcile schedules and budgets with safe and efficient ship operation
Write the ship-shore coordination record and proposed action ownership
Communicate final coordination actions to captains and shore colleagues
Update the liaison record with confirmed agreements and open issues

tasks.design: Configure native schedule, budget and issue views in {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, with a coordination template in {DOCS}. The engineer retains reconciliation and colleague communication, with records before and after the actual agreement.
tasks.previous_blocker: The liaison repeatedly gathers context and writes the same ship and action details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and action fields can reduce lookup and repeated documentation.
tasks.still_hard: Budget and schedule pressures must not override operational safety.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicts and recognise when an operating constraint cannot be traded away.
tasks.altitude: Make ship-shore agreements visible and traceable.

reach.learn: Keep agreed action ownership separate from unresolved proposals.

evidence.claim: Native ship-shore reference views and coordination templates could reduce clerical preparation; the saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario connects colleagues within the same organisation; their location aboard or ashore does not make communication act_external.

The engineer produces ship identifier, issue, proposed action, owner, date and unresolved conflict in s4, then agreement status in s6. Retained 14 and four hours include capture and checks. Missing agreement remains open rather than automatically accepted.
Use native views and templates first. No machine changes a sailing schedule, budget or ship operating instruction.
The record has no self-approval gate; the final-content check belongs to actual communication in s5.
unknowns: Current ship-shore systems and whether repeated coordination records already use shared fields.
research_questions: Can native views and templates reduce lookup and writing without losing unresolved operational conflicts?

already_counted.description: Write the coordination record and action ownership.

incremental.description: Maintain ship links and coordination fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact coordination actions and current ship context communicated to the captain and shore colleagues; changes are checked before communication.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=90, gross=10; upkeep=2 gives central net=8. Reconciliation and communication retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain engineering activity, expense and equipment-maintenance records.

steps.what: Collect engineering activity, expense and repair source records
Align source fields with engineering department record categories
Write mapped expense and maintenance details into the department records
Check recorded details, resolve unmatched records and correct errors
Add engineering activity context and unresolved maintenance remarks

tasks.design: Configure supported source-field mapping from {ERP} and maintenance records into the department register in {OPS_SYSTEM}, with native context fields. The engineer selects evidence, checks the import and adds the activity meaning that structured fields cannot supply.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source expenses and equipment work details are aligned and rekeyed into a separate department register.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable source identifiers and supported import mapping can remove duplicate transfer.
tasks.still_hard: A maintenance entry can exist without establishing what work was actually completed.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve mismatches and distinguish evidence of expenditure from evidence of repair completion.
tasks.altitude: Keep department records tied to their actual source evidence.

reach.learn: Preserve equipment, work-order and source-document identifiers.

evidence.claim: Supported source-field mapping and native record import could reduce duplicate engineering administration; feasibility and saving remain an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The baseline contains real mapping and rekeying into a separate department register; no saving is assigned to merely saving an existing record.

Producer contract: expense owners produce date, amount, currency and receipt identifier; maintenance technicians produce equipment identifier, work identifier, date and action. The engineer collects and checks these sources in s1 with all 25 hours counted, and captures context in s5 with eight retained hours. This design does not require new supplier or colleague capture.
Missing source identifiers, conflicting amounts or ambiguous equipment links stop the affected write and enter manual resolution in s4. No system infers repair completion.
Use native import and record fields first. No payment, maintenance release, external send or author self-approval gate is proposed.
unknowns: Supported exports, current source completeness and existence of a separate duplicate register.
research_questions: Can the import preserve source identifiers and stop duplicate or ambiguous records on a representative sample?

already_counted.description: Check imported records and resolve mismatches.

incremental.description: Maintain field mappings and regression-check imports.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 separate-register scenario: B=100, R=48, gross=52; upkeep=8 gives central net=44. Existing integrated records would reduce the gain sharply.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Oversee prototype construction and basin tests and develop checked hull curves and data.

steps.what: Oversee construction of the hull prototype against the intended design
Oversee model basin testing and investigate unusual prototype behaviour
Record prototype condition, basin results and measurement caveats
Prepare sectional geometry, waterline inputs and mass-distribution assumptions
Calculate sectional and waterline curves, center of gravity, buoyancy and stability data
Assess ideal hull form and document curve and stability limitations

tasks.design: Use native test-record fields in {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET}, and repeatable hydrostatic calculations in naval design software represented by {OTHER}. The architect supervises construction and testing, supplies checked geometry and mass assumptions, then interprets and documents the results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test records and repeated curve and hydrostatic preparation take time around prototype oversight.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable geometry and mass inputs permit tested repeat calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Model-scale behaviour, input assumptions and unusual test results require engineering interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether apparently favourable curves describe a defensible hull design.

ambition.what: Compare another checked hull variant without repeating manual curve preparation.

tasks.altitude: Keep physical prototype evidence connected to hull-form judgement.

reach.learn: Keep scale, loading and departures tied to each run.

evidence.claim: Tested hydrostatic routines and native test-record fields could reduce repeated preparation; this prototype-work saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Construction oversight, test oversight, measurement recording, curve inputs, calculation and written assessment are all counted separately.

The architect produces prototype identifier, scale, test date, loading, run results, units and departures in s3, with 12 retained hours including capture. The architect produces hull offsets, waterline positions, mass distribution, coordinate convention and calculation options in s4, with all ten hours counted.
Missing geometry, inconsistent units or unclear loading stops calculation for manual correction and investigation in s6. OTHER means existing naval CAD or hydrostatics software.

Use native calculation tools first. Calculation savings apply only to repeated manual curve or input preparation today; existing automatic solver runtime earns no saving. No prototype release or external send is proposed.
unknowns: Existing hydrostatics automation and actual manual curve preparation.
research_questions: Can the routine reproduce a known hull's curves and hydrostatic results while detecting scale and coordinate mismatches?

already_counted.description: Prepare and check geometry and mass inputs.

incremental.description: Maintain calculation inputs and regression-check known hull cases.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 manual-preparation scenario: B=100, R=77, gross=23; upkeep=6 gives central net=17. Construction and test oversight retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep crew competence, ship-shore coordination and prototype judgement human while reducing duplicate records and calculations.
reach: Link crew training, operational agreements, source records and prototype evidence.
role.ambitious_version: A marine engineer who can trace each operational or design conclusion to observed work and checked evidence.
